stories.headline: Kansas City Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy thriving in expanded role as Seahawks loom
stories.summary: The Chiefs will likely need similar improved play -- or even better -- from Worthy in Sunday's showdown vs. Seattle.
stories.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- When Chiefs receiver Xavier Worthy entered Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, he knew the team's offensive game plan was different for him.

"They told me all week it's going to be for me, and I've got to step up for the receiver room," Worthy said of the coaching staff following the Chiefs' Week 6 win against the Los Angeles Chargers. "Guys are down, so I did my job."

The proof was demonstrated in the Chiefs' opening possession. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes' first passing attempt was for Worthy. As the game progressed, the Chiefs' need for Worthy to have a strong performance increased. Tight end Travis Kelce, Mahomes' most reliable pass catcher, sustained a right ankle injury in the first quarter.

Mahomes responded by trusting Worthy -- and the receiver kept rewarding the Chiefs. In his best performance of the season, Worthy, a third-year player, finished Sunday's game with a game-high seven receptions for 73 yards. The Chiefs' offense needed Worthy's production, too, especially since it was Mahomes' first game this season without his top receivers: Tyquan Thornton, who was placed on injured reserve last week after suffering a dislocated left ankle, and Rashee Rice, who is recovering from a strained right hamstring.

Worthy on Wednesday compared getting targets early in Sunday's game that led to positive receptions when a basketball player swishes multiple shots in the first quarter.

"You hit five in a row [in basketball], it doesn't get any better than that," Worthy said, smiling. "It obviously built the confidence and led to a strong game."

The 5-0 Chiefs will likely need similar play -- or even a better performance -- from Worthy in this Sunday's showdown against the Seattle Seahawks (3-3), the NFL's defending champion.

For much of his career, Worthy has tried to become the speed threat many had hoped after he broke the record for the 40-yard dash at the 2024 NFL combine (4.21 seconds). He showed sizable improvement as a rookie, recording 638 receiving yards and nine total touchdowns. But last season was a disappointment. He sustained a significant right shoulder injury on opening night when he collided with Kelce while running a crossing route.

Coach Andy Reid acknowledged the Chiefs had to adjust the routes Worthy ran last season to better protect his shoulder. He finished with 532 receiving yards and one touchdown.

"People look at him because he's a little bit smaller and he's real fast, so they think of him as just a deep threat," Reid said of Worthy, who is listed at 5-foot-11 and 165 pounds. "We've always looked at him like he can run shallow crosses, deep crosses. He can do all that stuff and [is] very good at it. He's tough and he's smart, so you can move him around a lot in a lot of different spots."

In Sunday's game, Worthy caught the ball on crossing routes, beating zone and man-to-man coverage on different snaps. When the Chiefs asked him to work in the intermediate area of the field, he was able to create proper separation. All told, he led the team with 28 routes.

Worthy never dropped the ball, either. He made multiple diving catches, becoming the Chiefs' first pass catcher this season to have a plus-17.1% catch rate over expected and a 100% catch rate with at least five targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

"Xavier had another good day," Mahomes said Sunday. "If he keeps stacking those, it'll help out a ton, as we get Rashee back."

In September, Reid and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy called plays that manufactured short receptions for Worthy, hoping his speed could be used to create explosive gains. Instead, Worthy was unable to outrun defenders or break tackles on the perimeter. In the Chiefs' first three games, he recorded 10 receptions on 15 targets for just 63 yards.

The biggest moment for Worthy during that month was when he ran a deep route on opening night against the Denver Broncos. Instead of running his route in front of the two safeties, he kept sprinting to split the defenders in hopes Mahomes would throw a deep pass for him to run under. Instead, Mahomes threw an intermediate pass that was intercepted.

"I thought one thing, he thought the other," Worthy said the following week of his miscommunication with Mahomes. "We both weren't wrong, but it's about getting on the same page and knowing what each other is going to do. It was a newer play that we didn't get a lot of reps of, so it's about understanding what [Mahomes] would rather like in [that] situation."

Since the calendar flipped to October, Worthy has been a more effective receiver. The Chiefs beat the Las Vegas Raiders in part because Mahomes was able to find receivers downfield against man-to-man coverage. Worthy ran a deep over route when the Raiders blitzed in the first quarter and made a contested catch for a 41-yard gain.

"I'm building momentum," Worthy said. "As a receiver, just getting that momentum and getting that first catch. That first deep ball, I felt like that's what unlocked it for me -- and I feel they trust me, just going out there and executing. Having the trust of your team is big."

Worthy's role should continue to grow since Thornton is expected to be out until January.

"Me and Pat [are] building that relationship and [it's] me feeling stronger and better each and every week, just continuing to be that reliable target for Pat and making his job easier," Worthy said Wednesday. "If I go out there and do that, everything's going to come."

With more opportunities from Mahomes likely, Worthy is eyeing the first 100-yard receiving game of his career. After beating the Chargers, Worthy was satisfied to make a bigger impact in the Chiefs' continued success.

"We're 5-0 -- and it's hard to be 5-0 in this league," Worthy said. "I feel like we're playing some of our best ball. Whatever I can do, whether it's getting targets or not, or taking two [defenders] or blocking in the run game for [running back Kenneth Walker III], I'm going to do it."

stories.headline: Ruben Amorim with 'nothing to say' about Man United on return to England
stories.summary: Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.
stories.body:
Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 14 months in charge, and was appointed by the Serie A side in June.

Amorim revealed he does not think he has changed as a person since his time with the Red Devils, but believes he has become better at his job.

"Overall, I think the important thing is that I'm here as AC Milan's manager," said Amorim, speaking at a press conference at the Vitality Stadium and quoted by Milan News.

"I have nothing to say about United. I can say that I loved the club and the atmosphere: what happened doesn't change that.

"Then I moved on, now I'm at AC Milan and I'm focused on this: at every big club, problems are always around the corner. I focus on ourselves and I don't think about the teams. My past at United doesn't matter; what I said when I signed there remains the same."

Amorim revealed Samuel Chukwueze is out with a hip problem, and Gonçalo Ramos has sustained a calf strain, and expects 19-year-old Alphadjo Cissè, who he believes has reached only "50 per cent of his potential" to feature in Thursday's line-up to face the Cherries.

"I have more experience as a coach, but I'm not a different person," Amorim added, reflecting on his spell with United.

"I understand football better, and that will help me deal with problems in the future. I think I'm the same person, just a little more experienced in some things."

The man who replaced Amorim at United, Michael Carrick, has seen his position come under serious pressure in recent weeks as the club have endured a torrid start to the new season.

His team were beaten 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' Como in Italy on Wednesday in a match that saw Carrick and Fernandes appear to trade barbs through their post-match comments to the travelling media.

stories.headline: Valverde and Güler show why they'll be key for Madrid in Sunday's Clásico
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé has warned that "not much" should be read into Madrid's dismantling of RB Leipzig ahead of Sunday's Clásico, but Jose Mourinho is surely starting to figure out who his best XI is.
stories.body:
MADRID -- What can Real Madrid take from their 4-1 win over RB Leipzig into Sunday's Clásico with Barcelona? If you believe Kylian Mbappé, not much.

"It's completely different," he told Movistar, speaking seconds after the final whistle in Wednesday's UEFA Champions League game at the Bernabéu. "We've only thought about tonight's game. The team hasn't thought about Sunday yet."

Still, watching Madrid dismantle Leipzig in the second half -- when goals from Arda Güler, Mbappé and Yan Diomande followed Bernardo Silva's first-half tap-in to ensure a comprehensive win -- it was impossible not let your mind drift towards the implications for Camp Nou.

Is Federico Valverde now Madrid's first-choice right-back, ahead of two specialists in Trent Alexander-Arnold and Denzel Dumfries? Will coach José Mourinho risk Güler in central midfield, or play it safe and shift him out to the wing? And is Diomande now certain to start, having followed his brilliant goal against Sevilla on Sunday with another, even better strike off the bench?

- As it happened: Como stun Man Utd, Real Madrid run riot over RB Leipzig

- United players were abysmal, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

- Watch El Clásico LIVE, 10/25, 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

"It's been 105 days that I've been here, it isn't many," Mourinho said post-match. "I need to get to know [the players], and the best place to do that is on the pitch, in competition."

Earlier this season, Mourinho had been insistent about Valverde's role. "He can play [at right-back], it's happened in the past, but for me, he's a central midfielder," the coach said in August.

Wednesday's performance, Valverde's second in a row at right-back, suggested otherwise. There were moments of discomfort, like when he was beaten early on by Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa. But after that, he barely put a foot wrong. Over 90 minutes, Valverde had the most touches (115) of any player on the pitch. He completed the second-most passes, after Dean Huijsen.

At one end, he created three chances, playing three key passes, including the cross from which Silva scored, after Güler's shot fell to him. At the other end, no player had more defensive interventions (12, to Huijsen's 11), which includes tackles, interceptions and clearances.

In other words: Valverde was everywhere. After a performance like this, it's hard to imagine him not staying at right-back against Barcelona.

The only player who rivalled Valverde for influence in Madrid's play was Güler. In just the last week, in games against AS Roma, Sevilla and Leipzig -- all respectable opposition -- Güler has contributed two goals and two assists. Against Leipzig, Güler just beat Valverde to the most passes played into the final third, with 27 to Valverde's 26.

He played here on the right wing, and the only question on Sunday is whether Güler stays there, or returns to the centre, in a more attacking, ambitious formation, which might go against Mourinho's instincts.

"[Valverde and Güler] played well on the right-hand side," Mourinho said. "They're good solutions."

There is also the question of finding a place for Silva, who has featured little this season, but deserved his confidence-boosting goal, after a display which showcased his ability to link up the play, always looking for the ball, and then able to turn and find space.

The suspicion is that Silva will be back on the bench on Sunday, but he, and Güler, make the team better.

"It's that balance between having the ball and controlling the game, and also being an intense team," Silva admitted on Wednesday. "It's difficult. I'm ready to help the team, if it's five minutes, 10 minutes or 90 minutes."

And then there's Diomande. Earlier in the season, the teenage winger's minutes were limited, with Mourinho cautiously integrating Madrid's record signing into his plans.

He now has three goals and three assists since the international break, and Wednesday's goal was the best of the lot, volleying a Brahim Díaz cross effortlessly into the top corner.

"He has a lot to improve," Mourinho said just this week. "He's young. He's still naive, he's still the unfinished article. At Real Madrid the demands are high ... He reminds me of Vinícius [Júnior] when he arrived."

Diomande is now meeting those demands, and the contrast with Vinícius is stark. The Brazilian was replaced by Diomande after 70 minutes, having again struggled to make an impact. Vinícius is unavailable for the Clásico, as his domestic ban continues.

"The intention of bringing [Diomande] on wasn't thinking about the Clásico," Mourinho insisted. "It was thinking about this game. I knew a fresh Diomande, coming on with half an hour left, is difficult. His speed is important.

"For me, Vini had a good game. He could have scored a great goal, and their keeper made a great save. I wouldn't say he's sad, that's a feeling only he can explain, but his coach is happy."

Otherwise, Wednesday's lessons repeated things we already knew. Mbappé is back on form -- with four goals in a week -- and Thibaut Courtois might be Madrid's most consistently important player.

"The only thing I didn't like was [Leipzig's] goal, which Courtois didn't deserve," Mourinho said. "When you make two saves like he did at 0-0, you don't deserve that your teammates ruin it."

The final scoreline meant Madrid go into the Clásico having scored 12 goals in a week: 4-3 at Roma, 4-1 against Sevilla and Leipzig.

They have the firepower; and in goal, they have Courtois. The doubts are elsewhere, above all in midfield.

"For the Clásico, confidence doesn't exist on a scale of one to 10," Mourinho said. "Saying it's a game like all the others would be a lie."

stories.headline: WNBA Finals live: Valkyries-Dream Game 3 analysis, updates and highlights
stories.summary: The Finals resume with Game 3 as Atlanta hosts Golden State. ESPN is courtside at State Farm Arena with analysis.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Two days after their first WNBA Finals win in franchise history, the Atlanta Dream host Game 3 on Wednesday (8 p.m. ET).

The No. 4 seed Dream upended the No. 2 Golden State Valkyries on Monday at Chase Center to tie the series at 1-1. Atlanta now hosts the next two games before the best-of-seven Finals return to San Francisco for Game 5 on Monday.

State Farm Arena, which seats more than 17,000 fans, is expected to be a sellout Wednesday. The Dream have played all of their playoff games there this postseason, as well as six games in the regular season.

In Game 2, a 79-65 Atlanta win, Angel Reese had 30 points and 16 rebounds. In Game 1, defense and Gabby Williams' 26 points led Golden State to a 68-64 victory.

Both teams are seeking their first WNBA championship. Atlanta has played in three previous Finals but was swept in each appearance. Golden State is making its first trip to the Finals in just its second season.

ESPN will be courtside and providing live analysis throughout Game 3.

stories.headline: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani won't require surgery, expected to pitch in 2027
stories.summary: Shohei Ohtani will not require surgery to treat any ailment he dealt with this past season, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday. And: "I fully expect him to pitch next year," Friedman added.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani will not require surgery to treat his left knee or right arm or any other ailment he dealt with throughout the second half of this past season, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday.

Doctors merely prescribed rest. The expectation is that his 2027 season will be unaffected. When Ohtani begins his preparations for it, he will train as a two-way player.

"I fully expect him to pitch next year," Friedman said during an end-of-season news conference at Dodger Stadium.

But what that looks like has yet to be determined.

"This is unprecedented, what he's doing," Friedman added. "So obviously for us it's unprecedented. We don't have any experience to draw from. We can't go look at how other situations have played out to try to learn from the good and the bad. We have to all just figure it out together. And I'm not only expecting him to pitch; we're excited about him pitching. So now it's about: How do we do that? How do we manage through a long season and have him at his best going into October? That's a challenge."

Ohtani was a diminished version of himself by the time October arrived. He ended the regular season with 11 hits and 29 strikeouts over his last 70 at-bats and went 4-for-22 with no extra-base hits in his first seven postseason games. Ohtani finally broke through with a home run in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series, his first since Aug. 18, but it was too late for a Dodgers team that was ultimately swept by the Milwaukee Brewers.

Asked if the Dodgers could have managed Ohtani's two-way status differently to put him in a better spot for October, Friedman said: "I don't know the answer to that. It's one of those things that -- the injuries started in early July. Through mid-August, he was still I think the consensus MVP."

Ohtani went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in his first 14 starts, striking out 95 batters and issuing 26 walks in 85⅔ innings. But continual pain in his left knee and right biceps prevented him from pitching beyond July 3. As of Aug. 18, he was slashing .294/.390/.558 with 30 home runs and seven stolen bases. But physical discomforts started to merge into his at-bats, ultimately throwing his mechanics out of whack. Ohtani was not put on the injured list until after Labor Day, giving him only five regular-season games to get reacclimated to major league pitching before the playoffs.

Speaking after the Dodgers' season-ending 6-4 loss on Oct. 15, Ohtani said he was "not quite satisfied with how things shaped up on the pitching side."

"I haven't been able to really come to grips with what I've learned overall this season," Ohtani added through an interpreter. "It's something that I'm going to go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training programs and see what I can come up with for next season."

Ohtani was attempting his first full-time two-way season in three years, and doing so at age 32 proved more difficult than at 29. Friedman acknowledged that Ohtani's offensive struggles "certainly had an impact" on the Dodgers' early exit. But the entire offense slumped, combining to post a .590 OPS in the postseason and go 4-for-27 with runners in scoring position in the NLCS.

Friedman announced there would be no changes to Dave Roberts' coaching staff and said it was "business as usual" with owner Mark Walter, who is under federal investigation over alleged multibillion-dollar self-dealing.

"We talked to Mark after we lost," Friedman said, "and he was obviously really disappointed. But so much of his focus was on, 'OK, what can we do? What are our plans?'"

The Dodgers' brain trust hasn't necessarily figured that out just yet.

At the forefront of their minds will be the pending free agency of Tarik Skubal, the ace pitcher they acquired before the trade deadline, as well as several important relievers, most notably Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips. Along the way, Friedman and his group will try to figure out how to inject some youth into baseball's oldest position player group.

But nothing will be more important than their plan with Ohtani -- specifically how they handle his pitching so that he makes an impact on the mound without it affecting his offense.

The Dodgers could opt to start his season as a pitcher later, or work in more off days in between, or perhaps some combination of both. For this to work, several people within the organization believe, Ohtani will have to be more forthcoming with his ailments. One question the Dodgers haven't seemingly figured out is how much autonomy Ohtani will have over how this plays out.

One thing seems certain: Friedman, and perhaps the Dodgers as a whole, value his pitching enough to give it another try.

"I think we're just going to have to be very deliberate about it on all sides," Friedman said of the back-and-forth communication, "because the value of it is incredible, and therefore it's incumbent upon all of us to figure out the best way to do it."

stories.headline: Brady Tkachuk returns to Ottawa for first time since trade
stories.summary: Brady Tkachuk is playing in Ottawa for the first time asking for and getting a trade from the Senators.
stories.body:
OTTAWA -- Brady Tkachuk will face his former Senators team for the first time as a member of the Florida Panthers on Wednesday, after requesting a trade out of Ottawa last spring.

And while the club's former captain isn't likely to receive a warm welcome, Tkachuk goes into the night at peace with himself over how his uncoupling with Ottawa played out.

"I know for me, I was able to look myself in the mirror up until that final game [in Ottawa], knowing that I put so much blood, sweat, and tears into this team and into this organization," Tkachuk said after the Panthers' morning skate on Wednesday. "There was stuff out there [in the media] that wasn't true and I guess questioned where my mind had been at for the last little bit [leading up to the trade]. That was probably the hardest part of this process, with how untrue that was, but getting past that ... I'm excited for this next chapter."

Tkachuk does see Wednesday as a chance to truly turn the page. He arrived early to the visitors side of Canadian Tire Centre -- about three hours before Florida's scheduled ice time -- just to catch up with the Senators' staff. Tuesday, Tkachuk also dined with several former teammates -- and yes, he picked up the check -- with whom he has stayed close from an eight-year stint in Canada's capital.

The Senators' fan base, however, could have a less positive reaction to seeing Tkachuk back in their building.

It was late last April, following Ottawa's first-round playoff sweep by Carolina, that Tkachuk spoke publicly about the "frustrating" questions regarding his commitment to the Senators and doubled down on his loyalty to the team.

Behind closed doors, though, Tkachuk approached general manager Steve Staios about wanting out. Tkachuk still had two years remaining on a seven-year, $57.5 million contract that included a full no-movement clause, and he was willing to waive it for the opportunity to join his brother Matthew and the Panthers.

So, Staios shipped Tkachuk off in June in exchange for a trio of first-round draft picks (two in 2026 and a conditional in 2029) plus a 2027 second-round selection. Tkachuk left town with the fifth-most points in franchise history (463 in 572 games) and fourth-most goals (213).

The disconnect between Tkachuk's words and actions has been a sticking point for fans and made his departure even more painful. Tkachuk reiterated that there were private "personal and professional reasons" he shared with Staios about his request and wasn't open to sharing them. That leaves Tkachuk's motivations open to interpretation. But he's not concerned about his own feelings getting hurt.

"Everyone is entitled to their opinions; whatever emotions there may be, they're entitled to that," Tkachuk said. "I know for me, [a negative response] is not going to be taken personally. I know how I feel about this city, about this fan base, and how thankful and appreciative that I am. It's not going to change how I feel."

There isn't much Tkachuk can do to control how the fans respond to his presence, anyway. He will attempt to be altruistic in the face of their displeasure, though. Tkachuk told Matthew on Tuesday's episode of their "Wingman" podcast that any of his old No. 7 Senators sweaters tossed onto the ice during Wednesday's game will get rounded up and donated to Ottawa's local Boys & Girls club.

And it helps that Tkachuk is going into an important Atlantic Division battle on a heater. After tallying zero points in his first six games with the Panthers, Tkachuk exploded with consecutive natural hat tricks to give him six goals and 10 points through nine games.

There is a resignation, almost, in Tkachuk in the hours leading up to Wednesday's return. He laughs at having stayed in a local hotel prior to a game for the first time since his rookie development camp and spoke wistfully of how he'll share memories with his grandkids someday of the time he spent with the Senators. One way or another, the homecoming is over with early in his Panthers tenure and should, he hopes, allow everyone to move on with him into this new phase of his career.

"You can't really control the past at this point," Tkachuk said. "Just have to accept it and move on to the next chapter. I loved my time here. I loved not just my time on the ice; I loved everything about the community. There are relationships [built] that will last a lifetime...I gave absolutely everything I had. So hopefully, that's my legacy here."

stories.headline: Lando Norris vows to make 'better decisions' after Oscar Piastri clash
stories.summary: Lando Norris has vowed to make "better decisions" going forward after further talks with McLaren over his collision with teammate Oscar Piastri in Singapore.
stories.body:
Lando Norris has vowed to make "better decisions" going forward after further talks with McLaren over his collision with teammate Oscar Piastri in Singapore.

Norris made a clumsy move on Piastri on the final lap of the sprint race at Marina Bay, spinning both McLarens around and costing the team eight points.

The reigning world champion was initially flippant and sarcastic to media when asked about the incident, but following talks with McLaren team boss Andrea Stella and CEO Zak Brown, he rowed that back and accepted blame.

The team held further meetings in the week between Singapore and this weekend's U.S. Grand Prix and Norris has said he will strive to improve going forward.

"I take responsibility for my mistakes, and I learn from them," Norris said in McLaren's preview for the upcoming Austin race.

"This team is my motivation every weekend, and my aim is to repay the hard work everyone puts in by improving, making better decisions, and representing the team in the best possible way."

McLaren's rules of engagement between its drivers has been a recurring talking point over the past few seasons of Formula 1.

- Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri collision at Singapore GP sprint 'not acceptable' - McLaren boss

- Norris takes responsibility for collision with Oscar Piastri in Singapore: 'I let McLaren down'

The team dubbed it 'Papaya Rules' after Piastri and Norris nearly collided at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix and the issue rumbled through into the following season as they became title rivals.

That season had two notable flashpoints involving contact: Norris drove into the back of Piastri at last year's Canadian Grand Prix, while Piastri was held accountable for an incident at the start of the sprint at the U.S. Grand Prix 12 months ago which took both cars out of the race.

McLaren has been unable to replicate last year's championship winning form, with just two wins so far -- both via Norris, in Hungary and the Netherlands either side of the August summer break.

stories.headline: Blanchfield out, Suarez and Jandiroba move up in pound-for-pound rankings
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
Virna Jandiroba has a fight coming up on Nov. 7 and an opportunity to prove her worth as a top-10 women's fighter.

Jandiroba enters the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings this week without having fought since April, because previously ninth-ranked Erin Blanchfield lost at UFC Edmonton over the weekend. Moving up one spot to No. 9 is Tatiana Suarez, who faces Jandiroba in two weeks.

Jandiroba is the new No. 10 after receiving support from three of the five ESPN panelists. The other two voted for Jasmine Jasudavicius, who beat Blanchfield on Saturday, and bantamweight Joselyne Edwards, winner of five fights in a row.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 21. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: Nov. 7 vs. Virna Jandiroba

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

10. Virna Jandiroba

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 23-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Tabatha Ricci, April 4

Next: Nov. 7 vs. Tatiana Suarez

Jandiroba fell short in last October's fight with Mackenzie Dern for the vacant title, but she bounced back in April with a victory over Ricci. Up next is a top-10 showdown with Suarez, who also lost a title challenge last year. The winner will be right back in the championship mix.

Other fighter receiving votes: Joselyne Edwards and Jasmine Jasudavicius.

How our panel voted

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?
stories.summary: The Ballon d'Or awards are typically tough to predict, but can ESPN and our global resources do just that?
stories.body:
The destination of the Ballon d'Or is typically tough to predict. Just ask Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who, in 2024, had spent weeks believing he would win the men's award only to learn hours ahead of the ceremony that it had gone to Manchester City midfielder Rodri instead.

This year, it is no less straightforward.

On the men's side, there are plenty of candidates: Teenager Lamine Yamal dazzled for Barcelona, Harry Kane scored more goals for Bayern Munich than he ever has before, Kylian Mbappé starred for Real Madrid, while the 2026 World Cup saw Lionel Messi and Rodri compete to be named the competition's best player (in the end, it went to Rodri).

And for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Alexia Putellas is the favorite after captaining Barcelona to another quadruple, but she was far from the only world-class player on that team.

The winners for both will be revealed on Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London, alongside a number of other awards, but is there a way to gauge who will walk away with the prizes ahead of time?

The men's Ballon d'Or is decided by a group of 100 journalists, each from different countries, while the Ballon d'Or Feminin's voting roll is made up of 50 journalists from 50 different countries. We decided to replicate that voting with ESPN journalists stationed all over the world.

Here's how we did it:

Methodology:

ESPN has a global team of journalists in every corner of the globe. We asked 20 ESPN journalists from around the world -- one per country -- to submit a ballot.
We used the official Ballon d'Or shortlists.
We had each voter submit their top five for the Ballon d'Or and their top three for all other awards.
Like official awards, each first-place vote received 15 points, followed by 12 points for second, 10 points for third, eight points for fourth and six points for fifth.

So, in a global experiment, can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or?

Jump to:

Ballon d'Or | Women's Ballon d'Or

Other awards

BALLON D'OR: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona, RW

What our voters said:

Josué Utrilla, ESPN Guatemala reporter: "I believe that being a world champion -- while playing a key role in Spain's attack and enjoying excellent form with Barcelona in LaLiga -- demonstrates the talent he possesses at such a young age (19) and has earned him a place among football's biggest stars."

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich, ST

What our voters said:
Tom Hamilton, ESPN UK senior writer: "Okay, he didn't win the World Cup, or the Champions League, but Kane's year is unsurpassed. He scored 73 goals in 65 matches across the England national team and Bayern. It's a freakish record, the like of which we'll never see again. Let's park sentimentality and aesthetic-influenced bias; this award rewards individual brilliance."

Thijs Zwagerman, ESPN NL reporter: "Despite scoring goals at an extraordinary rate for years, Kane still does not receive the full recognition he deserves on the international stage. His qualities extend far beyond his remarkable goal-scoring record. He possesses the rare ability for a striker to drop deep, influence the game from a deeper position and operate like a playmaker as well. While Kane has yet to win the Champions League or the World Cup, that does not diminish his individual brilliance. In my view, he was still the best player in the world on an individual level."

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami CF, FW

What our voters said:
Anirudh Menon, ESPN India editor: "If this award is to be given to the best footballer on the planet, there can only be one answer. He may be 39 years old; he may even be playing in Major League Soccer (where he did win the MLS Cup and topped almost every attacking chart in the league), but the 2026 World Cup showed just how vast the gulf between Messi and everyone else remains. When he turns it on, there isn't anyone close. Give him his ninth Ballon d'Or already."

Teo Coquet, ESPN Argentina reporter: "I choose him because of his attacking influence and ability to remain decisive on the international stage. His performance for Argentina at the World Cup is also a key factor in my evaluation. At 39 years old, he has played one of the best World Cups of his career."

Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid, ST

What our voters said:

Omar Flores, ESPN Mexico reporter: "Mbappé was the leading scorer across every competition he played in during the 2025-26 season, topping the charts in both the UEFA Champions League and Spain's LaLiga. At the World Cup, the France star scored 10 goals and became the tournament's all-time leading scorer (22 goals). Although he was unable to help his team advance beyond the semifinals, he remains one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d'Or. "

Carlos Valdez, ESPN Colombia reporter: "I would put Mbappé first because of his extraordinary ability to make the difference at the highest level. His pace, finishing, consistency and capacity to deliver in decisive moments make him one of the most influential players in world football. His goal-scoring achievements across the league, Champions League and World Cup further strengthen his case. For me, the Ballon d'Or should recognize not only outstanding numbers, but also a player's ability to change the course of a game, and Mbappé embodies that quality."

Fabián Ruiz, Paris Saint-Germain, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain reporter: "If we forget about the cameras, the spotlights, the commercial interests, and all the pomp that increasingly accompanies the business of football, then Ruiz should win the Ballon d'Or. I have no doubt about it. Why? It's simple. He was an undisputed and fundamental player for PSG's repeated Champions League title success last season, and was equally fundamental for Luis de la Fuente's victorious Spain side at the 2026 World Cup when Pedri wasn't at his best in midfield. Ruiz won it all over the past 12 months and was a standout player. He lacks marketing appeal, which will work against him, but he would be a deserving winner."

Rodri, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Jean Beausejour, ESPN Chile analyst: "In a World Cup year, winning the tournament carries enormous weight. Rodri had a tremendous influence on Spain's performances on football's biggest stage. Spain's ability to dominate matches, control the tempo and impose their style of play against different opponents was largely down to Rodri's intelligence, positioning and exceptional ability to dictate the game. His influence went far beyond individual statistics, making him, in my opinion, the most deserving candidate for the Ballon d'Or."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: HARRY KANE

In a symbol of how divisive the men's Ballon d'Or race is, Kane received half of the first-place votes but only one of the other 10 voters put him second. Perhaps the biggest surprise was the large snubbing of Yamal, who received just a single No. 1 vote.

This was a two-horse race and, as ESPN writer Bill Connelly wrote earlier this month: "Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal."

There is a slice of history on offer for Kane, too: Kane would be just the fifth Englishman to cradle the golden trophy, alongside Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

BALLON D'OR FEMININE: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES
Alexia Putellas, London City Lionesses, AM

What our voters said:

Leonard Solms, ESPN Africa reporter: "In her final season at Barcelona, midfield maestro Putellas not only captained Barcelona to the Liga F, UEFA Women's Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España trophies -- but also scored 20 goals and assisted 14 in 43 games. Capable of filling multiple roles in the team, Putellas is the kind of player any manager would love to have 11 of, and her brilliance should not be taken for granted."

Marissa Lordanic, ESPN Australia editor: "Putellas was once again invaluable across multiple competitions. The epitome of a big-game player, she ensured Barcelona's trophy case continued to grow before she tested herself in a new league."

Ewa Pajor, Barcelona, ST

What our voters said:

Gustavo Hofman, ESPN Brasil reporter: "Pajor combined outstanding individual production with collective success and delivered when it mattered most. She recorded 34 goals and eight assists in 46 appearances for club and country, helping Barcelona win the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup. Her intelligent movement and clinical finishing gave Barcelona a cutting edge throughout the season, but her Champions League performances ultimately put her ahead of the competition: she finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals and scored twice in the 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes in the final."

Ed Dove, ESPN Africa reporter: "In recent years, Pajor's performances haven't always been rewarded with the silverware and honors one might expect. That changed last term, where she was a key influence -- and a major goal threat -- in Barcelona's historic Quadruple-winning campaign. A genuine big-game player, she scored 33 across all competitions, including 11 in the Champions League, where she struck in every knockout round Barca played in before netting twice in a one-sided final victory over OL Lyonnes. Pajor may have scored fewer than she did during his remarkable debut season at Barca, but after overcoming the UWCL final defeat by Arsenal in 2025, she deserves the individual recognition here."

Temwa Chawinga, Kansas City Current, FW

What our voters said:

Jeff Kassouf, ESPN (US) reporter: "No player changes a game like Chawinga. She can create chances on her own in one-vs.-one situations from literally inside her own half on the counter attack, and is a sharp goal scorer. Scoring 20 goals in the NWSL and then following that up with 15 the next season is dominant form at a world-class level. And she does it for club and country, having helped lowly Malawi to the 2027 World Cup. This time next year, more international opponents will know the fear of having Chawinga run at their defense."

Patri Guijarro, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain: "The backbone of Barcelona's women's team and an excellent midfielder who makes runs from the second line. Other players usually steal the spotlight, but her talent is unquestionable. She makes the rest of the team shine."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: ALEXIA PUTELLAS
This result is not a surprise. Putellas is the clear favourite for the award, and our voters agreed.

Putellas enjoyed a dream end to her 14-year Barcelona career last season, captaining the club to a second Quadruple in three years, including lifting the Women's Champions League, before she moved to captain London City Lionesses, who are now third in the Women's Super League after five games.

Should Putellas actually win, she would earn her third Ballon d'Or award, joining former Barcelona teammate Aitana Bonmatí as its most frequent recipient.

OTHER AWARDS

3. Yan Diomandé (Real Madrid, Ivory Coast)

2. Luis Enrique (PSG)

1. Pere Romeu (Barcelona)

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return; Panthers lock in Patea
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Rivals monitor Patea as open market looms
Penrith young gun Luron Patea is expected to test the open market from November 1, with multiple clubs keeping tabs on the promising prop.

Patea is contracted until the end of 2027, but the Panthers are yet to begin talks over an extension, leaving rival clubs poised to explore a deal for 2028 and beyond.

Penrith have not granted Patea permission to negotiate with other clubs before November 1.

The Panthers junior made his NRL debut in 2024 and has shown promise during his first-grade opportunities, providing another emerging option in Penrith's forward pack.

He is among several Panthers players approaching the final year of their contracts, with veteran prop Moses Leota also unsigned beyond 2027.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Bucs QB Jalon Daniels swaps jerseys with idol, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers
stories.summary: Following Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime victory, Jalon Daniels left with a keepsake from his idol, Aaron Rodgers.
stories.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- All last week, teammates of Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels urged him to do it.

"I was talking to the quarterbacks beforehand and they basically were just like, 'If you get the opportunity to ask him, you better ask him,'" Daniels told ESPN.

Fellow Buccaneers quarterback Brett Rypien told Daniels, "If you didn't ask him, I was going to ask for you," Daniels recalled.

They were talking about Daniels meeting his idol -- Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who on Sunday led Pittsburgh to a 26-19 come-from-behind overtime victory over the host Bucs -- and asking for a jersey.

"Last season, last go around for him. So, I had to ask before he got up out of here," Daniels said, referring to Rodgers' plans to retire following the 2026 campaign.

Daniels summoned the courage to do so and was met with a long embrace, which was captured on camera postgame and showed a tender side to Rodgers not often seen because of his intensity in games.

"I mean, it was kind of crazy," Daniels said. "So, just kind of ... without trying to completely ask that -- I don't want to be that guy -- and he was just like, 'I know exactly what you're getting at. I'll give you the jersey.' And then I'm like, 'All right man, thank you.'" The pair shook hands. Daniels then heard something he never imagined: The Super Bowl winner and future Pro Football Hall of Famer wanted his jersey too.

"[I] was about to walk away and he was like, 'Wait, hold on. Can I get yours?'" Daniels recalled Rodgers asking. "Now, that's kind of what caught me by surprise."

What Daniels didn't know was how much Rodgers knew of and respected his game from afar. The week prior, the 2026 undrafted free agent led the Bucs to a 24-16 primetime upset at the Dallas Cowboys. It was the Bucs' first victory of the season and just Daniels' second career start, which came unexpectedly after starter Baker Mayfield suffered a dislocated right thumb in Week 3.

"I appreciate the respect," Rodgers said of Daniels on the CBS broadcast. "Super respectful guy. I like his game. I like the way he throws it. Obviously, super talented with his feet. I'm excited to see how he develops. Learning behind a guy who's played a long time like Baker is obviously going to be great for him."

Daniels was touched by the praise.

"I respect that, as well," he said. "It's not every day you hear that from a Hall of Famer."

Rodgers' ability to perform in high-pressure situations, make passes from different angles, get out of the pocket and throw off-platform were elements Daniels tried to bring to his own game as a six-year starter for Kansas -- after Daniels was initially supposed to redshirt. Daniels' career as a Buccaneer began in similar fashion by not hearing his name called at all during draft weekend and starting Bucs training camp fourth on the depth chart. He moved all the way up to No. 2 by beating out veteran Jake Browning -- who had previously started 10 career games for the Cincinnati Bengals -- by giving the Bucs an offensive spark in the preseason.

Daniels said the moment with Rodgers "absolutely" lifted his spirits.

At one point Sunday, Tampa Bay was leading 16-3. But Rodgers mounted a fourth-quarter comeback while the Steelers' defense clamped down. Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions, and the Bucs fell to 1-5.

"It wasn't easy," Daniels said, "but it comes with the game."

stories.headline: 'Delighted' Aston Villa relishing UCL challenge after 3rd straight win
stories.summary: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery believes the confidence of his players is improving after they continued their impressive start to the Champions League campaign with a 3-1 victory over Viking.
stories.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery said the confidence of his players is improving after they continued their impressive start to the Champions League campaign with a 3-1 victory over Viking FK.

Villa Park is becoming a fortress in Europe and they have now won their last 12 major European home games and made it three from three in this year's Champions League.

They picked up their latest win thanks to Ross Barkley's opener and Emi Buendía's penalty, as well as an own goal from Henrik Heggheim.

- Champions League recap: Como stun Man United, Bayern-Arsenal share points

- Mbappé and Diomande delight, Vinícius Jr. whistled in Madrid win

- Carrick hits back at Fernandes criticism after Como rout Man United

Villa would have finished the night top of the Champions League table but for Viking's Peter Christiansen replying late which also denied them a third straight clean sheet.

Emery said there is still work to do but his side took another step forward.

"We are delighted how we are responding in our demands," he said. "Respecting the competition, respecting the opponents and how we are improving things.

"Through those issues I think we played a good match, serious match. Respecting them and following the plan we set up, then individually the players trying to display their quality.

"Today mixing those objectives, I think we did a good job and some players they did one step forward in their confidence, feeling better and understanding tactically and playing football."

Villa have won twice in front of their own fans in the Champions League but are still waiting to open their home account in the Premier League, which Emery hopes will come against Manchester City on the weekend.

"We are challenging each match as a objective to get better to become consistent in Europe and playing matches in the Premier League and trying to be very demanding," he added. "How we must feel strong and confident.

"I think there is still work to do, we did a very good match and Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points.

"Two matches winning here at home. In the Premier League we are still not winning but in Champions League league winning two good matches against Fenerbahce and today and now can feel confident and comfortable for the next challenges.

"The atmosphere was fantastic how we are enjoying Champions League with our supporters and enjoying together."

Viking boss Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim saw his side draw with Bayern Munich last week but were blown away in the first half by Villa a week later.

Aarsheim was happy with the way his side responded in the second half but says they had too much respect for their Premier League opponents before the break.

"Second half was much more like Viking wants to be," he said. "Maybe we had too much respect in the first half, they were all over us and didn't create much which is really rare for Viking.

"In the locker room, we talked [that] we have to be braver with the ball and did much better with the ball. We ended up drawing 1-1 in the second half -- that is something we can build on."

stories.headline: Inside the Boca training camp that spurred the Dream's WNBA Finals run
stories.summary: During the World Cup, the Dream headed to Florida for training camp, where DeWanna Bonner bonded with her new teammates.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- At the end of August, the Atlanta Dream had won five of six games, including four on the road, and were closing in on the right to host the first round of the WNBA playoffs. Within two weeks they knocked off the defending champion Las Vegas Aces and the presumptive favorite to win this season in the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx, with star Angel Reese recording her single-season record 29th double-double.

The Dream looked like one of the best teams in the league -- and then everything came to a screeching halt: The WNBA season paused for 17 days for the FIBA World Cup.

Reese and teammate Rhyne Howard headed overseas to compete for Team USA, with Atlanta reserves Isobel Borlase (Australia) and Sika Kone (Mali) also making their way to Berlin. But the rest of the Dream roster later met up in a coastal Florida town about 45 miles north of Miami, known more for beaches and shopping and retirees and snowbirds than basketball.

Amid the prolonged disruption to the WNBA season that threatened to kill momentum for teams, the Dream used the time to fortify theirs -- thanks to a mini training camp they held in Boca Raton, Florida, during the second weekend of the FIBA break.

"It was one of my [most] favorite trips of my career," said DeWanna Bonner, a 17-year veteran. "That was the best trip. It was so fun."

It's no coincidence the Dream have won 10 of 11 games since the break, including Monday's bounce-back Game 2 victory that tied the best-of-seven WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. Atlanta's 10 consecutive wins entering Game 1, which dated to that Aug. 30 victory over the Lynx, matched the 2017 Los Angeles Sparks for the longest win streak going into the Finals in league history.

The run coincides with Bonner's late-season signing, not insignificant in its own right. But the bulk of Atlanta's hot stretch has also followed the Boca trip, where Bonner -- who joined the Dream on Aug. 27 after a contract buyout with the Phoenix Mercury -- integrated into the team and the group came together before the most important part of the season.

"You'd see people [together] that you never thought would hang out with each other -- that's just how Boca brought us closer," second-year guard Te-Hina Paopao said. "And when the people from FIBA came back, it was just like nothing was missed."

Added Bonner: "It's just been up from there with us, and we've been locked in since then."

The Florida trip was far from a midseason vacation. The Dream had some of their best, most intense practices of the season at Florida Atlantic University -- where the team had also trained during the 2024 Olympic break. They scrimmaged against male practice players and, without any games to rest for, had a real opportunity to go hard up and down the court.

They held daily film sessions and drilled down on the defensive principles that made them one of the best units in the league. And with Howard and Reese abroad, other players were able to step up and get more of a run.

"Everybody was just challenging everyone, and everybody was motivating everyone," Bonner said, "and then we got off the court, and we got to go to the beach and love on each other a little bit. It was a great balance."

The trip was planned well before Bonner's arrival -- forward Naz Hillmon suggested it and several staff and front office members agreed it was a good idea -- but the timing proved fortuitous as Bonner was more fully incorporated into the mix.

"I think that break came at a great time for us," coach Karl Smesko said.

"Even though she's been in the league for a long time, coach uses a lot of different words in comparison to other coaches, so you have to pick up on that lingo," Hillmon said. "His style is a little bit different, but it was great that we had a little bit of a head start and not just throwing DB in [at the end of the regular season]."

Bonner had played one game with Atlanta before the break, so Boca allowed her to better learn Smesko's system and make up for lost time with most of her new teammates. That's when, Paopao said, she felt Bonner take her under her wing and start getting in her ear.

"They kind of grilled me a little bit, and I grilled them," Bonner said with a laugh. "We got a chance to understand what each other wants and each other's goals."

Getting to decompress and slow down a bit amid the in-season grind was a welcomed break ahead of the playoff push.

"[Boca] is a very quiet, very old town type of community," said Paopao, who said she enjoyed the shopping in the area. "It was a very nice pace for us, and nothing too crazy."

In Atlanta, players are more likely to go their separate ways when practice is over, but the opposite was the case in Florida. Players spent time together at the beach and pool, where they'd watch their teammates' World Cup games. One group of players and team personnel squeezed in an 18-hole golf outing, where point guard Jordin Canada served as Allisha Gray's caddie.

One memorable team dinner featured a lively WNBA trivia battle organized by general manager Dan Padover. A team that included Bonner and Canada won -- but guard Shatori Walker-Kimbrough still says her team was robbed over a technicality.

"I feel like when we're in this setting [at home], we've got friends, we've got family. Obviously, we connect off the court, but it was a little bit more sitting by the beach and talking for a little bit longer," Hillmon said. "It was definitely a great change of scenery and building a bond on and off the court."

Before this year, the Dream hadn't advanced past the first round of the playoffs since 2018, years before the first key player of their current roster would arrive in Atlanta. The Finals is new territory for young stars Howard, Hillmon and Reese.

But their veteran core of Bonner, Canada and Walker-Kimbrough has combined for five WNBA titles at previous stops. Those three, along with assistant coach LaToya Sanders (who won a title with the Washington Mystics in 2019), shared what it takes to win a championship at the end of those FAU practices.

Canada, the Dream's X factor this postseason and a two-time champion with the Seattle Storm, said she sees achieving that on- and off-court chemistry as one of those essential qualities.

"The championship teams I've been a part of, we've gotten to know each other off the court," Canada said. "We've hung out, had team dinners, just doing anything that we can to build bonds. And I think that means a lot more when you get to know this group on a deeper level outside of basketball and knowing who they are as people and what makes them go."

Now, between Canada's standout play, Reese's brilliance and what was forged in that long weekend in Boca, the Dream are three wins away from winning a championship -- not just with each other, but for each other.

"In moments like this, when you're in such a heated moment or a heated series, you want to fight and you want to battle for the girl to the left and right of you," Canada said, "because you know them on a personal level. You know them on a deeper level. And you want to do it for them."

ESPN's Kendra Andrews and Kareem Copeland contributed to this report.

stories.summary: The offseason carousel is in motion. Here's who is out -- and who could be in line to replace them.
stories.body:
The first 100-loss season in Los Angeles Angels franchise history meant the end of the line for skipper Kurt Suzuki.

The second managerial change since the end of the regular season came Monday when the Angels announced they would not pick up Suzuki's 2027 club option and will instead begin a search for a new manager.

Suzuki joins Dan Wilson, who told reporters last month he would not be returning as skipper of the Seattle Mariners.

Which major league teams will change managers next? And who could be next in line?

ESPN will track all of the managerial hirings and firings -- and provide potential top replacements for every opening as they happen.

Los Angeles Angels
2026 manager: Kurt Suzuki (Oct. 21)

Suzuki lasted just one year as Angels skipper.

A former catcher, Suzuki played the final two of his 16 big-league seasons (2021-22) with the Angels, then signed a one-year deal to manage the team last October.

Los Angeles' 62-100 mark in 2026 represented the first 100-loss season in franchise history, and a 10-game drop-off from the 2025 team, managed by Ron Washington and Ray Montgomery.

Longtime Angels owner Arte Moreno sold the club to Stan Kroenke in September. Kroenke won't officially take over until the first quarter of 2027.

Whether interim general manager John Mozeliak will continue with the team remains to be seen.

Seattle Mariners
2026 manager: Dan Wilson (Sept. 27)

Wilson is out in his second full season in Seattle after being hired in August 2024 to replace Scott Servais.

The Mariners entered the 2026 season as division favorites and a potential top American League contender coming off a 2025 playoff run that saw them eight outs away from the franchise's first World Series appearance before falling to the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 7 of the ALCS. Seattle got off to a slow start, with just four wins in its first 13 games. With season-long struggles from big stars like Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez, coupled with inconsistent pitching and an underperforming offense, the Mariners never got to more than four games over .500 on the season.

"This season has been very difficult, and of course the results have not been what any of us had expected," Wilson said after Sunday's 7-3 win over the Angels. "As a result, it was concluded that today is my last day as manager of the Seattle Mariners."

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.
